basics.name: Qinglin Meng
basics.label: PhD Candidate in Computer Science
basics.summary: Research in reinforcement learning, large language models, statistical machine learning, multi-armed bandits, and mechanism design.

highlights: Developed an LLM embedding and KNN retrieval pipeline for cost and profit prediction, reducing MAE by 15–20% relative to the existing economics-based baseline.
Post-trained a Transformer embedding model with contrastive learning.
Formulated incentive allocation as an MDP.
Developed offline RL algorithms for service quality and incentive cost.
Built a pipeline covering offline training, evaluation, online experimentation, and serving.

researchProjects.name: Reward-Free RL for Mechanism Design and Dynamic Pricing Optimization
researchProjects.advisor: Advisors: Michael I. Jordan, Zhaoran Wang, and Zhuoran Yang
highlights: Studied online mechanism design with linear function approximation.
Developed reward-free exploration over a rich policy space to estimate prices.
Designed optimistic/pessimistic Q-function approximation algorithms to recover mechanisms over repeated interactions while balancing seller and buyer profit.

researchProjects.name: Adaptive Training Data Allocation for LLM Safety via Non-stationary Bandits
highlights: Built a data pipeline with OpenFDA drug data, synthetic patient profiles, and generated scenarios for LLM safety evaluation and training.
Formulated adaptive post-training data selection as a non-stationary multi-armed bandit problem.
Implemented sliding-window Thompson Sampling to prioritize failure-prone drugs, reducing mean and worst-case error relative to uniform sampling and baseline curricula on LLaMA-3 and Qwen-2.5.

researchProjects.name: Near-Optimal Bandit Learning for Multiclass Classification
researchProjects.advisor: Advisors: Steve Hanneke and Shay Moran
highlights: Proved a sharp Sauer lemma based on the list-DS dimension.
Developed a chain-of-list learning algorithm achieving near-optimal sample complexity for multiclass learning with bandit feedback.
Improved an existing list-learning sample complexity bound by a factor of K⁵.

researchProjects.name: A Survey of Architecture-Level Design for Interpretable LLMs
highlights: Analyzed architecture-level interpretability techniques, including codebook features, sparse mixture-of-experts architectures, and sparse autoencoder based steering.

researchProjects.name: Reduction for Multiclass Learning
highlights: Studied multiclass reductions with potentially infinite label spaces.
Developed a representation preserving agnostic-to-realizable reduction by applying a realizable learner to realizable subsets of the input sample.
